To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and tested a novel parameter selection method that accounts for the model structure and the measurement set and that we have shown that the proposed method outperforms an alternative method based on the FIM.
a new parameter-selection method based on PCA is proposed and shown to be superior to the FIM method in a case study.

the parameter selection method based on principal component analysis of the parameter-output sensitivity matrix yields superior parameter estimation results than the method based on the Fisher Information Matrix.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and evaluation of a simple parameter-selection method for dynamic models.
the development of a methodology for the selection of model parameters for the purpose of on-line estimation.
the problem of model parameter estimation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method proposed herein is superior to the FIM method for this example, and is also more general and applicable to any type of model.
the method presented here has the potential to be a useful tool for the selection of parameters for off-line identification of mechanistic dynamic models.
the proposed method provides a simple and effective means of identifying the parameters most amenable to estimation from a given set of data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed parameter-selection procedure is simple, easy to use, and computationally inexpensive.
we have developed a new method for selecting parameters for off-line estimation that accounts for both model structure and data availability.
a good parameter selection method can be obtained by using the FIM, and that a good parameter-selection method is the one that is simple, and does not require the computation of the FIM.
The main takeaway from our work is that

parameter-selection techniques based on the FIM are not always optimal for off-line parameter identification, and the selection of parameters for off-line identification should be performed in a manner that is independent of the data.
the FIM-based approach is not always superior to other methods for parameter selection, especially in the context of mechanistic dynamic models.
a parameter selection method based on the sensitivity matrix is a simple, yet effective approach to select model parameters for offline estimation.
